diseases.name: Cescospora Leaf Spot
symptoms: Spots produced are small, numerous in number with pale brown centre and reddish brown margin. Similar spots also occur on branches and pods.
Under favourable environmental conditions, severe leaf spotting and defoliation occurs at the time of flowering and pod formation.
The fungus is seed-borne and also survives on plant debris in the soil.

management_practices: Spray Carbendazim 500 g/ha or Mancozeb 1000g /ha at initiation of the disease and 10 days later.
Water at the base of the plants using drip irrigation or soaker hoses to keep leaves dry, as wet conditions favor fungal growth.

diseases.name: Golden Mosaic
symptoms: small yellow flakes on the lamina during the initial infection stage which gradually increases in size to form green and chlorotic intermingled patches producing a yellow and light yellow patches and mosaic appearance.
Leaves may be reduced in size and may be curled.
Lower leaves are subjected to “mosaic burn” especially during periods of hot and dry weather.

management_practices: Sanitation is one of the common control methods for which includes removing the infected plants and weeds from field.
Rouging of young infected plants appears to reduce the amount of secondary spread within a field when incidences are low in the beginning of the season.
Crop rotation should also be employed to avoid infected soil/seed beds for at least two years.
Seed treatment with imidacloprid 70% WS @ 1g/kg of jute seeds and use of neem cake @ 250 kg/ha before sowing of the crop
foliar application with cypermethrin, deltamethrin and dimethoate 30 EC at 50 DAS proved quite effective in reducing the incidence of B. tabaci and thus also the virus infection.
Yellow sticky traps can be used to detect and monitor whitefly activity.
